reason: SCHEDULE/FEASIBILITY lens. It is refuted as written, although a repaired version can be scored in time. (1) The main route fails. 'Ride in the ladder kernel' inherits the ladder's branch dependency: the ladder runs only if #34 == 0.953 AND #35 >= #34, and its own schedule verdict is refuted, feasible=false, P(scored) ~0.42 (v_metric-math_div-budget-ladder-x138_schedule.json). (2) The validation as described cannot run on x138 geometry. No x138 lab cache exists. The two sibling plans to build one are rated P ~0.07 (x138-tail-lab-headcoords schedule) and P ~0.2 (divins-x138-lab-retune schedule), and both need 13-16 GPU-h plus friend A. The only runnable lab is replay.py on the exp39/exp48-equivalent B20 cache (laptop CPU). That cache has the pre-head detector coordinates, while the head moves nodes by 0.74 um on average and up to 1.61 um (v2 feasibility verify). So the lab is a proxy, and the 4.5 um threshold stays unvalidated on x138. (3) The idea's numbers are overstated. '25% of 43 FP' is the 4.0 um figure (11/43). At the proposed 4.5 um the lab removes 6 FP / 0 TP = 14% (research/wf_ideas_v2/r1_research_fork-midpoint-filter.json l.6). The upper bound is therefore about 1.8x too high, and v2 put the public gain at +0.0005..+0.0009 for 4.5 um. (4) Nothing is built yet. tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 accepts only divinsert and leafprune. grep finds no forkmid or FM45 code, and v2's planned 'FM45_sd on e48' verification never ran. A new patch is needed. It is mechanically easy: x138's add_safe_divisions_postlink edges carry safe_division=1 with edge_prob None, and div_insert marks div_inserted=1, so the 'safe-div only, not DaughterNet' selector exists in the kernel. The existing knob BIOHUB_OUTPUT_DIVISION_GEOMETRY_FILTER is a different rule (parent/sister distance on all forks, before linefit), so there is no zero-code --set route. Estimate: 1.5-2.5 h of agent work including tests, plus about 0.5 h for the same patch on the exp39 base in case #34 does not reproduce. (5) Schedule, if repaired, is not the binding constraint. There is no training, no new weights or dataset, and no friend A. The dummy run is about 40 min on a T4 (experiments/RESULTS.md row 67). Runtime is O(forks), negligible against the 12 h limit. The GPU dummy run can only start after the 26 Sep 00:00 UTC quota reset (vitaliineibauer has ~0 GPU-h now). That leaves 26 Sep 06:00-10:00 submit -> scored 26 Sep 15:00-20:00, i.e. about 60 h of slack for up to 2 retries. (6) The adoption rule 'adopt if >= base' is decided by noise. The expected effect is +0.0005..+0.001 against LB noise of about 0.003 and 3-decimal rounding, so a standalone probe carries almost no information. P(some scored LB probe containing the rule before 29 Sep 10:00) for the repaired path is 0.95 (patch + tests) x 0.85 (proxy lab gate passes) x 0.85-0.9 (user OKs a slot or a bundle) x 0.97 (dummy clean + scoring within 12 h, with retries) ~0.67-0.70. Without the proxy gate it is about 0.78; via the ladder bundle it is ~0.4.
